r10-deviation5.title: Deviation 5 - changed pre-existing assertion
r10-deviation5.imperative: Independently judge whether the changed --self-test assertion (claude.md -> CLAUDE.md) is genuinely stricter, whether matching is still case-insensitive while reporting is as-cited, and whether this is the ONLY pre-existing assertion altered. The assertion was not changed to green a failing test - it HAD to change once the reporting behaviour was corrected, and it was changed in the direction that catches the bug the old one pinned. r11-deviation6.title: Deviation 6 - re-measure CONTENT_HASH_RE
r11-deviation6.imperative: Re-measure the declined CONTENT_HASH_RE fix by execution. Does ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ already reject 65- and 128-char digests? Would {64,} loosen the pin? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r11-deviation6.finding: Deviation 6 CONFIRMED - the declined fix really is a false positive; the g1 re-review survivor should close as NOT-A-DEFECT. Re-measured by execution against the shipped is_content_hash: len63->False, len64->True, len65->False, len128->False. The decisive comparison: a 128-char sha512 under the SHIPPED ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ is rejected (False), and under the PROPOSED ^[0-9a-f]{64,}$ it is ACCEPTED as a sha256 pin (True). The implementer is right on both halves - the $ anchor already rejects longer digests, and {64,} would LOOSEN the pin. Taking the addendum's 'free fix' would have introduced the very hole it claimed to close. I also probed two behaviours the implementer did not report, and both are correct-by-design not holes: uppercase 'A'*64 returns True and leading/trailing newlines return True because is_content_hash applies .strip().lower() before matching (hex digests are case-insensitive; whitespace trimming is deliberate) - and an EMBEDDED newline correctly returns False, so there is no multiline escape. No finding.
